summary: Pise Point AWS on Kings Mountain, San Mateo County: a 1942 plan for an air and fire warning tower; FFLA lists it gone, and no source describes the site now.

facts.design: Air and fire warning lookout tower (planned 1942)
facts.status_note: FFLA lists it as gone; the sources read give no removal date

events.note: San Mateo County defense council's executive committee authorized $1,700 for an air and fire warning lookout tower on top of Kings Mountain (item dated August 11, 1942); the tower was to be erected at once

evidence.supports: August 1942 authorization of $1,700 for a lookout tower on Kings Mountain overlooking Half Moon Bay
evidence.quote: Payment of $1700 for an air and fire warning lookout tower on top of Kings mountain overlooking the Half Moon Bay area was authorized

evidence.supports: the authorization was made by the county defense council's executive committee
evidence.quote: at a meeting of the San Mateo county defense council's executive committee

evidence.supports: the tower was planned at Pise Point and was to be erected at once
evidence.quote: the new lookout tower would be erected at once at an eminence called Pise point

evidence.supports: planned staffing by members of the county civilian defense organization under Army supervision
evidence.quote: manned chiefly by members of the county civilian defense organization

evidence.supports: the tower would be under Army supervision
evidence.quote: it will be under army supervision

evidence.supports: the site is listed as AWS and fire
evidence.quote: San Mateo County - AWS and Fire

evidence.supports: AWS was a civilian service of the Army Ground Observer Corps during World War II
evidence.quote: was a civilian service of the United States Army Ground Observer Corps established during World War II

evidence.supports: AWS was set up to keep watch for enemy planes
evidence.quote: established during World War II to keep watch for enemy planes

evidence.supports: FFLA lists the Pise Point AWS lookout with status gone
today the spot is a map directory's scenic viewpoint, not a described structure
evidence.quote: Pise Lookout is a scenic viewpoint

evidence.supports: the viewpoint is situated near the Phleger Estate nature reserve
evidence.quote: situated nearby to the nature reserve Phleger Estate

notes_for_editor: Only one detailed source (Forest Lookouts, quoting the San Mateo Times of August 1942). The 1942 item is a plan; no source I read confirms completion, a date of removal, or what stands today. The Forest Lookouts page is titled Pise Point (Kings Mtn), and the existing record us-ca-pise-point-kings-mountain (west_us_lookouts source, GNIS approximate coordinates) looks like a duplicate about 4.5 km away; consider merging. The FFLA list gives this record's coordinates as 37.45564, -122.34154. A search snippet (not read) shows an FCC microwave license with a 'PISE LOOKOUT' transmit site; the FCC page returned 403, so that is unverified and worth checking for what remains on the site. The roles vocabulary has only 'aws', so the 'fire' part of the Forest Lookouts header is not recorded. Record kind 'unknown' could be 'tower' per the 1942 item; left for the editor.
